findings.evidence:
`pkg/planner/core/task.go:1356` `handlePartialOrderTopN` pushes `PhysicalLimit{Count: p.Count+p.Offset, PrefixCol: p.PrefixCol, PrefixLen: ...}` into `copTask.IndexPlan`, while `estimateMaxXForPartialOrder()` returns `0` (only used for stats).
`pkg/planner/core/operator/physicalop/physical_limit.go:153` `(*PhysicalLimit).ToPB` only sets `tipb.Limit{Limit: p.Count}` and never serializes `PrefixCol/PrefixLen` (same for `pkg/planner/core/operator/physicalop/physical_topn.go:205` TopN).
Integration test explicitly does not verify correctness yet: `tests/integrationtest/t/planner/core/partial_order_topn.test:441` (“TODO: Verify it after executor PR merged”).
findings.fix:
To make this safe before executor/protocol support lands, do not push a hard `Limit` into `copTask.IndexPlan` for partial-order TopN (keep scanning and let a TiDB-side TopN short-circuit once implemented), or implement full plumbing:
- Encode partial-order truncation into the cop request (e.g., populate `tipb.Limit.truncate_key_expr` on newer tipb) derived from `PrefixCol/PrefixLen`.
- Add executor support to read `N + all rows with same truncated key` so the TopN sees a correctness-preserving superset.
findings.impact: When `tidb_opt_partial_ordered_index_for_topn=COST` is enabled and a prefix index is selected for `ORDER BY ... LIMIT`, the pushed-down index-side `Limit` can truncate the input to `Count+Offset` rows even though prefix indexes do not fully order by the column. This can return incorrect rows (violates ORDER BY semantics) for cases where multiple rows share the same indexed prefix but differ beyond the prefix length.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`: `handlePartialOrderTopN` still pushes a `PhysicalLimit` and `(*PhysicalLimit).ToPB` still does not populate any truncate/prefix field (even though tipb has evolved).
findings.verify: Add a regression test that executes (not just EXPLAIN) with a prefix index and values sharing the same prefix but different full values, e.g. two rows where scan order-by-handle conflicts with full string order, and assert `ORDER BY col LIMIT 1` returns the correct row under `tidb_opt_partial_ordered_index_for_topn=COST` + `force_index`. Repeat for ASC/DESC and with OFFSET.
findings.what: Partial-order TopN plan can produce wrong query results because the planner pushes a normal cop `Limit(count=Count+Offset)` on a prefix-index-ordered stream without any protocol/executor mechanism to include the extra rows needed for correctness within the boundary prefix.

findings.evidence:
Parent (`995d6f987c5a...`) sysvar accepted bool forms: `pkg/sessionctx/variable/sysvar.go` defines `tidb_opt_partial_ordered_index_for_topn` as `TypeBool` and validates `0/1/ON/OFF`.
This commit changes it to enum-only: `pkg/sessionctx/variable/sysvar.go:3073` sets `TypeEnum` with `PossibleValues: ["DISABLE","COST"]` and validation rejects `ON/OFF/0/1`; tests assert these now error (`pkg/sessionctx/variable/tests/session_test.go:757`).
findings.fix:
If backward compatibility is desired, accept legacy bool values as aliases:
- Map `ON`/`1` -> `COST`
- Map `OFF`/`0` -> `DISABLE`
while still returning/storing canonical enum values.
If strictness is intentional, document this as a breaking sysvar interface change and consider keeping a deprecated alias sysvar for older automation.
findings.impact: Compatibility break for existing automation/config/hints that set `tidb_opt_partial_ordered_index_for_topn` to `ON/OFF` or `1/0`; these now fail with `ErrWrongValueForVar` (MySQL error 1231), potentially causing query failures on upgrade.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` at `3b531d4e3d99cb988bebccb8f63a96afff0ec6cd`: sysvar remains `TypeEnum` and still rejects `ON/OFF/0/1`.
findings.verify: Add/adjust unit tests to cover legacy inputs mapping to canonical values and ensure `SELECT @@tidb_opt_partial_ordered_index_for_topn` returns only `DISABLE|COST` while `SET ... = ON/OFF/0/1` remains accepted (if compatibility is chosen).
findings.what: `tidb_opt_partial_ordered_index_for_topn` changes from BOOL to ENUM and drops support for legacy `ON/OFF/0/1` values, breaking sysvar/hint compatibility across versions.

subject: planner, core: implement partial order TopN attach2Task and partial order flow (#65799)
summary: Found a correctness blocker: the new partial-order TopN path pushes a normal cop `Limit(Count+Offset)` without any protocol/executor plumbing to fetch the extra rows required for prefix-index partial order, so enabling the feature can violate ORDER BY semantics. Also found a High compatibility break: sysvar `tidb_opt_partial_ordered_index_for_topn` changes from BOOL to ENUM and now rejects `ON/OFF/0/1`, which can break existing configs/hints.
